scope: Actual IDF5.4.4 ESP32S3 firmware selected configuration and linked paths, not generic MbedTLS3.6.5 clearance

rows.disposition: not applicable to qualified firmware path
rows.reason: No untrusted-user certificate enrollment or mixed-parser certificate registration exists. The bundle is compiled, but swarm_bridge HTTP configuration does not select cert_pem, crt_bundle_attach or use_global_ca_store; with insecure TLS disabled, HTTPS setup fails rather than registering attacker certificates. This is not a claim the parser is patched or that the optional HTTPS caller is currently a working qualified profile.
evidence: sdkconfig: certificate bundle default full; custom bundle disabled

rows.disposition: not applicable to qualified firmware path
rows.reason: No owned operation loads/derives a long-term MbedTLS ECC private key or performs deterministic ECDSA signing: outbound HTTP has no client-key configuration, and firmware artifact authentication uses separate Ed25519 verification. Ordinary ephemeral ECDHE and peer signature verification do not perform the repeated long-term-secret operations described by the advisory. NIST optimization is enabled, so future long-term-key use requires reassessment.

rows.disposition: not applicable to qualified firmware path
rows.reason: Maintained ESP32 firmware has no fork, VM snapshot or reusable hibernation image copying an initialized RNG state. Flashing the immutable firmware initializes a fresh runtime; it does not clone initialized process memory. This does not endorse adding runtime snapshot/resume cloning.

rows.disposition: not applicable to qualified firmware path
rows.reason: No owned RSA private-key decryption service/key configuration or PSA asymmetric-decrypt caller. Outbound TLS client RSA key exchange encrypts to the peer rather than serving an attacker-controlled private-decryption oracle.

rows.disposition: not applicable to qualified firmware path
rows.reason: The actual CONFIG_MBEDTLS_NIST_KW_C is disabled, so the Wi-Fi adapter excludes the MbedTLS CCM wrapper block and uses the supplicant fallback. The conditional wrappers at crypto_mbedtls.c831–877 are one-shot APIs even if enabled. No owned multipart mbedtls_ccm_finish caller accepts an arbitrary tag length; TLS one-shot/wrapper use is explicitly excluded by the primary advisory.
